result.one_liner: Shopify is an ecommerce platform whose Admin/Storefront APIs let developers build apps and integrations against merchant stores, authenticated via OAuth (or static access tokens for custom apps).
result.notes: Free Partner account + free development store give self-serve API credentials (OAuth access tokens or custom-app "Admin API access token") for building/testing immediately, no approval needed for that. Public App Store listing does require app review, but that's a distribution gate, not a credential gate, so access is scored self_serve_free rather than admin_approval. REST Admin API is now legacy (frozen at 2025-10 version, no new public apps allowed to use it since 2025-04-01) while GraphQL Admin API is the actively developed surface — flagged as a partial caveat inside api_type rather than a blocker since GraphQL fully covers the same functionality. Access tokens are sent in a custom `X-Shopify-Access-Token` header (not standard OAuth Bearer syntax), grouped here under api_key/oauth2 rather than adding "other". Vendor also publishes an official local "Dev MCP server" for docs/API discovery (no auth required) in addition to several community MCP servers seen in the registry hints.

evidence.quote: The merchant is redirected to Shopify to approve access, then back to your app with a code that your app exchanges for an access token.
Your app authenticates as itself with its client ID and client secret, and there's no merchant approval step.
The credential your code sends on each GraphQL Admin API request, in the `X-Shopify-Access-Token` header
The REST Admin API is a legacy API as of October 1, 2024. Starting April 1, 2025, all new public apps must be built exclusively with the GraphQL Admin API.
The Admin API lets you build apps and integrations that extend and enhance the Shopify admin.
If you prefer MCP, you can connect to Shopify's developer resources through the Dev MCP server. The server runs locally and doesn't require authentication.
